approach:
The root cause is that landing, history and attribution rules are derived from the happy-path commit shape (the job's own commits), and the only guard is planner/critic prose (planner.md line 16, critic.md line 14). Nothing runs where readings are accepted. The fix is a pure check, `check_history_fixture(reading)`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, added as one `step!` line in `refusing_check` directly after `check_code_survey`.

The check applies to a reading with a capability, no question, class `code` or `tests`, and at least one behavior criterion. These are the same gate conditions as `check_code_survey`, factored into a small shared helper. Within that gate it asks whether the reading touches a landing, history or attribution rule. It does if either holds:
- A non-delete deliverable under `crates/` has the file name `land.rs`, `history.rs`, `attribution.rs` or `invariant.rs`.
- A criterion contains one of the whole-word phrases `landing`, `history check`, `attribution check`, `commit shape`, `commit-shape`, `pr_commits`, `--history` or `--attribution`.

If it does, some Behavior criterion must name a realistic-branch fixture. After case, white space and apostrophe normalisation, that criterion text must contain `realistic` and `fixture`, plus all three shapes: `intervention commit`, `records-only commit` (or `records only commit`), and `job landing` (or `job's landing`). Otherwise the check bails with an error that starts "the reading was refused because" and says what to add.

The check reads only the Reading: no model call, no repository, no records, no network. The doc comment names the root cause and the three jobs (20261024-153908-1rve, 20261024-154552-e65v, 20261025-012657-hac3) and declares "expected 3% of newly refused readings". The 3% is an unmeasured estimate. The CHANGELOG records it and the replay at verification measures it.

Supporting edits:
- The `refusal_corpus` mechanism (`every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case`, refusal_corpus.rs line 1300) requires a refusing corpus case for every `step!` check, so the plan adds corpus cases.
- The one existing reading fixture that now trips the check (`ENGM_CRITERION`, reading.rs line 8483) gets the realistic-fixture criterion.
- An athena-context test ties the planner prose to the phrases the check requires.
- A test_support.rs doc paragraph tells test authors which shapes the shared fixture holds and which they must add.

This job does not change a landing or history rule itself. It changes a reading gate, so no commit-shape table applies. No classification function is touched (no `pr_commits` or trailer code), so there is no crate that calls one. The producer still runs the full `cargo test --locked`.

decisions.choice: Enforce at the reading-stage gate, as a new `step!(check_history_fixture(reading));` line in `refusing_check` after `check_code_survey`.
decisions.reason: All three failures started when a reading was accepted whose criteria never required a branch with more than job commits. `refusing_check` is the one seam every reading passes (`check_reading_acceptance` at reading.rs:3199, `check_reading_text` at 4622 for `athena check-reading` and the replay, and `Athena::read` at 663). A step there keeps the first-failure name derived from `stringify!`. `no_check_bypasses_refusing_check` and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` keep the check wired and covered. The new step does not sit between the governance/outcome_state or outcome_state/environment_reach pairs whose adjacency the tests at 8224 and 8700 pin.

rejected.option: Re-land the pr_commits classification or trailer cutover work in land.rs, gh.rs, invariant.rs, commits.rs
rejected.why: Those are the instances, and the brief drops them. Fixing one classification again leaves the next landing rule free to be tested only against job commits.

rejected.option: More planner/critic prose or a planner-side check
rejected.why: The guidance already exists as prose (planner.md:16, critic.md:14, and the lib.rs test) and failed three times. Planner and critic prompts are out of scope, and the planner has no mechanical gate.

rejected.option: Add a rule line to the reader prompt
rejected.why: The reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom (`budget reader: 1997 of 2000` in docs/system-facts.md), and `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` pins 7 rule lines. The refusal error tells the reader exactly what to add instead.

gh.rs holds pull-request creation, CI polling and landing, so this would refuse most unrelated code jobs. A `gh.rs` job that changes a landing check is caught by the criterion phrases (`landing`, `pr_commits`, `history check`).

rejected.option: Accept the shared `CutoverFixture` (test_support.rs) by name alone as satisfying the check
rejected.why: Its documented history (bootstrap, old-way job, cutover job through a pull request, import commit) does not by itself include an intervention commit. Naming it would again let a rule pass without the shape. The criterion must name the three shapes.

rejected.option: Require the retry-after-block landing shape as well as the three in the brief
rejected.why: The brief fixes the three (intervention, records-only, job landing). Adding a fourth raises the refusal rate beyond the declared estimate, and the planner prose already asks for it.

decisions.choice: Factor the gate conditions of `check_code_survey` (capability set, no question, class code/tests, at least one behavior criterion) into one private helper used by both checks.
decisions.reason: One definition of 'a code reading with a behavior criterion' avoids two copies drifting. The helper keeps exactly the current condition, so `code_survey_does_not_apply_outside_its_gate` (reading.rs:10063) still covers it.

rejected.option: Copy the condition into the new check
rejected.why: Two copies can drift and give inconsistent gating.

decisions.choice: The satisfying criterion must be a Behavior criterion and carry `realistic`, `fixture` and the three shapes. The error message states each of these and gives an example criterion.
decisions.reason: A fixture belongs to a test, so only a behavior criterion is a test demonstration. The three shapes are literally what the brief and planner prose require. A lexical check is the same kind `check_code_survey` and `check_environment_reach` use, and its limit (it cannot read a negation) is stated in the doc comment.

rejected.why: A content criterion cannot show a test run on a branch.

decisions.choice: Add corpus cases and two input-form tags to refusal_corpus.rs and update `INPUT_FORMS` from 30 to 32.
decisions.reason: `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` fails without a case in which the new check refuses. The system rule asks the planner to map each input form to corpus cases.

rejected.option: Rely only on unit tests in reading.rs
rejected.why: The corpus test would fail, because no corpus case refuses by the new check.

decisions.choice: The athena-context test in lib.rs reads reading.rs through `include_str!("../../athena-core/src/reading.rs")` and the planner frame text. It asserts that each shape phrase the check requires appears in `PLANNER_FRAME` and that the step line exists.
decisions.reason: athena-core depends on athena-context, so athena-context cannot call the check. A source-level test keeps the prose and the mechanism from drifting without a prompt edit, which is out of scope.

rejected.why: Out of scope, and it would move the budget lines in docs/system-facts.md.

risks.risk: Over-refusal: a code job that merely mentions 'landing' (for example in a criterion about an unrelated feature) is refused and costs a reader retry.
risks.mitigation: The trigger is narrow: class code/tests, a behavior criterion, and a landing source file or a whole-word phrase. Unrelated-reading tests assert the non-triggers, and the replay at verification measures the share, which is declared at 3% (estimate). If the share is above 10% without a declaration, the replay holds the job.

risks.risk: The reader cannot satisfy the check because it does not know the wording.
risks.mitigation: The error text gives an exact example criterion naming the fixture and the three shapes. Spellings with spaces or hyphens, and `job's landing`, are accepted. The reader prompt cannot be edited, so the refusal message is the teaching channel.

risks.risk: A criterion can name the shapes but the test uses a poor fixture, since the check is lexical.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment states the limit (lexical, no negation reading). The criterion must also be Behavior kind, and the verifier judges whether the fixture is real. A Content-kind criterion is not enough.

risks.risk: An existing test that builds a code reading with a trigger phrase breaks.
risks.mitigation: The ENGM fixture test is updated, and the producer grep for the trigger phrases in `crates/**/tests` and the `tests` module of reading.rs finds no other code-class behavior reading. The full `cargo test --locked` run catches any left.

risks.risk: A corpus case is refused by an earlier check, so the expected check name is wrong.
risks.mitigation: Cases are built from `base_reading` with one field changed. The new refusal cases set class code, a Behavior criterion and a `Code survey:` assumption so `check_code_survey` passes first. They are placed with the existing code-survey cases.

risks.risk: The cross-crate `include_str!` in athena-context breaks builds when the crate is built alone.
risks.mitigation: The `include_str!` path matches the existing cross-directory use of `include_str!("../../../athena.toml")` in reading.rs. If the cross-crate path does not resolve, the producer reads the shapes from a `pub const` that athena-context exports instead, with no prompt change.

Companion test `history_fixture_refusal_needs_the_step_line` greps the `refusing_check` body for the step and fails if it is removed.
